hero.summary: A live stage of how the work runs, framed by business value. Three lanes run at the same time: Harness (written briefs, isolated working copies, independent inspection), Production (automatic checks, releases, a report after every working session) and Speed (parallel fronts, fast decisions). All three feed one Throughput counter of delivered, reviewed work that keeps climbing, while the client's team keeps receiving releases and sending validations back. It never stops.

harness.title: Harness
cap: The working setup that makes AI-assisted building safe: written briefs, isolated working copies and rules the builders cannot cross.
Independent inspection, and every change traceable to a request.

production.title: Production
cap: What comes out is reviewed, checked and goes live: releases, not demos or prototypes.
Automatic checks on every change, and a written report after every working session.

speed.title: Speed
cap: Weeks, not quarters: fronts move in parallel, one builder each.
The lead decides fast because the harness carries the risk.

brief.title: Written brief

m.t1: the why and what done means

cap: Each front starts from a written brief: the why, what done means, the limits.
A builder never starts from a chat message.

copy.title: Working copy
cap: Each builder works in its own isolated working copy.
Guard rules block what a builder may not touch.

inspect.title: Inspection
cap: An independent inspector reads every delivery against its request and tries to break it.
It never edits what it inspects; findings go to the lead.

checks.title: Automatic checks
cap: Automatic checks run on every change, before anything moves on.

release.title: Release

m.t1: not a demo, not a prototype

cap: What comes out is a reviewed release that goes live, not a demo or a prototype.

report.title: Session report
cap: Every working session ends with a written report: what changed and what to test.

fronts.title: Parallel fronts
cap: Several fronts move at the same time, one builder each.
Weeks, not quarters.

decision.title: Decision
cap: A senior lead decides and writes each decision down.
Decisions come fast because the harness carries the risk.

throughput.title: Throughput
cap: Harness, production and speed together: a sustained volume of delivered, reviewed work, week after week.
The counter never resets.

The client's people review, validate and release; then the loop goes on. It never stops.

about.p1: With over 25 years in software engineering, I now ship production software through agentic workflows and build the guardrails that make them safe: in 2026 alone, more than 3,000 commits across about 40 repositories, 125 merged merge requests in ten weeks on a trade-marketing platform at GoAPICE, a 42,000-line CRM module for an ISP client, and Chordo Pro on the Apple App Store and the Microsoft Store.
about.p2: The AI engineering is hands-on: agent harnesses (guard hooks, quality-gate skills, parallel worktrees, adversarial review rounds) used daily across an employer, a client and my own products, CI guards for schema drift and contract freshness, and audits of my own practice run by agent fleets over thousands of real prompts.
about.p3: Before that: four years on the UI of H2O.ai's machine-learning platform, team lead for a North American e-procurement SaaS at BairesDev, lead architect of a telemedicine platform on four clouds, and six years at Microsoft Brasil.
about.languages: Languages: Portuguese (native) · English (full professional; working language since 2018) · Spanish (elementary)

goapice.desc: Own the backend, Protobuf contracts and offline-first Flutter field app of a trade-marketing platform: 125 merged MRs across five repositories in ten weeks, BFF tests 84 → 725, app tests 145 → 736, 21 tester builds in 24 days. Cut a 1.29M-row paged query from ~35 s to ~2 s by pushing LIMIT/OFFSET down to Trino in the Python query engine; redesigned a 46M-row out-of-memory aggregation to ~12 s per page. Benchmarked Trino against StarRocks on replayed production dashboard loads, led a compute-amplification audit across four services, built an AWS FinOps pipeline that surfaced savings worth 30–60% of monthly spend, and published 21 architecture pages through a Wiki.js publisher I wrote. Earlier in the year: 165 commits hardening the Golyzer React 18 / Vite / Module Federation modernization, a TipTap rich-text editor and a conditional-formatting engine. Run a governed multi-session Claude Code workflow (64 parallel worktrees, guard hooks, quality-gate skills) and wrote the team hook that keeps agents from approving or merging MRs.

isp.desc: ISP operations platform (React 19, TanStack, FastAPI, SQLModel, PostgreSQL, Redis). Sole author of the CRM module: a 28-table schema, 16 Alembic migrations, 105 FastAPI endpoints behind 103 RBAC capabilities, and a kanban, lead workspace and proposal editor with triggers and cadences — 115 commits and 42.8k lines, with 248 pytest functions, the repository's first Playwright suite (105 cases) and a 233-case client validation page. Introduced pull-request delivery to a team that merged straight to main; 23 merged PRs and 409 commits, the most of any contributor during the engagement. Built a guard-railed agent harness for client work (PreToolUse hook, critical-values scanner, pre-push LLM review, parallel agents in isolated working copies); a multi-agent pass took the TypeScript build from 100 errors to 0. 446 logged hours in five months alongside full-time employment, with 22 engineering reports in English.

proj.chordo: Cross-platform chord-sheet app, live on the Apple App Store (iOS, macOS) since March 2026 and on the Microsoft Store since September 2026. Renders ICLF chord sheets with syllable-precise alignment, a visual chord editor, a voicing calculator and instrument-aware rendering, on a custom music-theory engine with key detection and transposition. Six releases, 449 automated tests, fastlane and a CI release pipeline.
proj.alphatester: Multi-tenant feedback-to-fix platform: embeddable web and Flutter SDKs with an offline queue, API-key ingest, an RBAC dashboard with TOTP two-factor authentication, and automatic GitHub issue creation. Live collecting beta-tester feedback since August 2026. 243 tests, Terraform on GCP.
proj.geodome: Geodesic dome calculator and timber-frame designer: 1V to 6V, Class I and II, cut lists with compound bevels and a triangle-by-triangle build sequence, in eight languages. A pure-Dart geometry engine whose beam fit holds residuals under a micron; its algorithms passed a 41-finding multi-agent adversarial review.
proj.pdb: Community directory for a coastal village in Laguna, SC, Brazil. Helps locals and tourists find service providers, transport schedules, and trails. Offline-first with bundled data, SQLite WASM for web, responsive hero carousel, and trilingual support (Portuguese, English, Spanish).
proj.iclf: Inline Chorded Lyrics Format — an open plain-text specification for notating song lyrics with precisely positioned chords. Designed for human readability so musicians can open an .iclf file and play instantly. Supports syllable-precise chord alignment, extensible metadata directives, and accessibility for screen readers.
proj.parser: A Dart library that parses and validates ICLF files into structured data models. Classifies documents as valid, invalid, or recoverable — applying automatic corrections where possible. Includes a ChordMatcher for cross-ecosystem chord validation and a CLI for rendering chord sheets.
proj.musictheory: A Dart package and CLI providing programmatic access to music theory — notes, intervals, chords, instruments, voicing calculation, key detection, Roman numeral analysis, transposition, and capo suggestions. Serves as the theoretical foundation for the Chordo ecosystem.

homestead.desc: Four years of hands-on sustainable land management in the Atlantic Forest region of Santa Catarina. Practicing polyculture, permaculture, and agro-pasture-forest integration. Planting and nurturing native trees, caring for fruit and native sprouts with community donations, and active forest protection. Zero trees cut down, zero chemical inputs used. Learning and applying regenerative agriculture principles to restore and protect local biodiversity.
